message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic chills and modern scares you might enjoy for a Friday‑night movie marathon:

| # | Title | Year | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|---|-------|------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** (1980) | A psychological thriller set in an isolated hotel, featuring Jack Nicholson’s iconic descent into madness. |
| 2 | **Get Out** (2017) | A smart blend of horror and social satire that keeps you guessing until the very end. |
| 3 | **Hereditary** (2018) | A family drama that turns into a relentless nightmare; the dread builds slowly but never lets up. |
| 4 | **A Quiet Place** (2018) | Suspenseful, low‑key terror where silence is survival—great for a tense group viewing. |
| 5 | **Midsommar** (2019) | A daylight horror that subverts expectations with its unsettling folk‑ritual vibe. |
| 6 | **It Follows** (2014) | A fresh take on the “invisible stalker” trope, with a creepy soundtrack that lingers. |
| 7 | **The Conjuring** (2013) | Paranormal investigations turned cinematic; the atmosphere feels genuinely haunted. |
| 8 | **The Babadook** (2014) | Psychological horror that uses a child’s fear as a metaphor for grief and trauma. |
| 9 | **Suspiria** (1977) | A visually striking, surreal horror that still feels relevant today. |
|10 | **The Cabin in the Woods** (2012) | A meta‑commentary on horror tropes that delivers both laughs and genuine scares. |

Feel free to pick one or two from each era for a varied experience!
